properties.statement:
**THE MACHINE-WIDE INSTALLER HAS THE SAME DEFECT ALEX REPORTED ABOUT THE PROJECT INSTALLER — ONE LEVEL UP, AND INTO THE USER'S HOME DIRECTORY.** Measured on Anthony's own machine, 2026-08-14.

═══ ✅ THE EVIDENCE IS A FILE ON THIS MACHINE ═══

```
$ command -v opencode      -> absent
$ cat ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
  top-level keys : ["$schema", "mcp"]
  mcp entries    : ["reflow2"]        <- reflow2 and nothing else
  command        : […/target/debug/reflow2-mcp, --graph-path, .reflow2/graph,
                    --shared, --only-if-present]
```
⇒ **reflow2 CREATED an OpenCode configuration in the home directory of a user who does not have OpenCode installed.** The file holds no theme, no model, no other server — nothing but reflow2's own entry, which is what a file reflow2 wrote from scratch looks like. Anthony's primary agent is Claude Code.

═══ THE MECHANISM ═══

`tools/reflow2_install.py` registers unconditionally, with no harness question anywhere:
```
register_claude(binary)      -> global Claude config
register_opencode(binary)    -> ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
install_commands()           -> global slash commands (Claude-shaped)
install_hooks(nudge)         -> loop-nudge hooks (Claude only)
```
There is no `register_vscode`, so the coverage is not even uniform: **Claude and OpenCode are written for everybody; VS Code is written for nobody.**

═══ ⭐ WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE PROJECT-LEVEL CASE ═══

`cap:init-asks-which-harness` (built the same day) fixed `reflow2_init.py`, which writes into a REPO the user chose to point at reflow2. **This writes into `$HOME`**, where the user never pointed anything. `cap:machine-wide-install`'s own installer output was already softened once for exactly this reason — Alex reported *"Installing reflow2 for every project on this machine"* as ALARMING, and it became *"Making reflow2 globally available to projects on this machine"*. **The wording was fixed; the behaviour it was describing was not.**

📌 AND THE `--only-if-present` FLAG SHOWS THE PROBLEM WAS PARTLY UNDERSTOOD. A global entry carries `--only-if-present` so the server does not fire in directories with no graph — someone thought carefully about a global config being too eager at RUN time, and not at all about it existing at INSTALL time for a tool the user does not run.

═══ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED ═══

⚠️ Whether the OpenCode entry is HARMFUL or merely present. An absent binary means nothing reads it, so the cost may be limited to a file nobody asked for — which is precisely the complaint Alex made about the repo, and which was judged worth fixing there.
⚠️ Whether `~/.copilot/` (present, containing only `ide/`) is reflow2's doing or GitHub's. **Not reflow2's**: nothing in `reflow2_install.py` writes it.
⚠️ Whether the same shape exists for the global Claude registration — it is the primary harness for both users, so it has never been the wrong thing to write, and this measurement says nothing about whether it should be conditional.

⇒ **THE HONEST GENERALISATION**, and it is `req:init-installs-only-the-harness-you-name` with a wider scope than it was written for: an installer writes files for the harness the user has, and asks when it cannot know. The requirement names `init`; **the machine-wide installer was never in its scope and has the same defect.**
